title: Anthropic Revenue Hits $16.8 Billion in Third Quarter
summary: Anthropic PBC told prospective investors its third-quarter revenue hit $16.8 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, as the artificial intelligence company pushes ahead with plans to go public.

title: CoreWeave Risk Gauge Hits Record, Pricing 60% Odds of Default
summary: CoreWeave Inc.’s credit risk climbed to an all-time high Thursday as its high-yield bonds extended declines, rattled by the AI cloud-computing company’s plans to ramp up borrowing.

title: Anthropic Urged to Pause IPO for AI Safety by NYC Comptroller
summary: Anthropic should pause its initial public offering until it has fully addressed risks around artificial intelligence, according to New York City’s comptroller. A letter from Mark Levine addressed to Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei on Wednesday suggested the Claude developer should instead focus on addressing the unprecedented risks of the technology. Ed Ludlow reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Rocket Lab Falls After Neutron Rocket Debut Delayed to 2027
summary: Rocket Lab Corp. shares plunged after the company again delayed the debut of its more powerful Neutron rocket, pushing the vehicle’s first flight to 2027.

title: SpaceX’s Spectrum Purchase Exposes Risks for Big Telecom Stocks
summary: Telecom stocks have long been considered a relatively safe bet for investors, offering predictable growth, limited downside and healthy dividends. But a combination of competition from SpaceX and rising Treasury yields is threatening to upend that equation.

title: Santander's Ana Botin on US Growth, Debt, AI and the Global Economy | The David Rubenstein Show
summary: Santander Executive Chair Ana Botin sits down with David Rubenstein to discuss the bank's expansion in the US, including its recent acquisition of Webster Financial, and why she sees lack of economic growth as one of the biggest challenges facing the global economy. She also discusses US debt, the outlook for the US and European economies amid geopolitical uncertainty, and the impact of AI on banking and jobs. Botin is on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This episode was recorded July 13 in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Crypto Traders Are Already Betting on Ambani’s Big Jio IPO
summary: Jio Platforms Ltd.’s record-breaking upcoming initial public offering is already trading on crypto rails, giving investors a round-the-clock venue to bet on the company’s valuation even before its shares hit local Indian exchanges.

title: Dangote Cement Adds Goldman, UBS for November London Listing
summary: Dangote Cement Plc added Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and UBS Group AG as bookrunners for a London listing that it’s preparing as soon as November, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Amazon Debuts Revamped Bee AI Wearables, $12-a-Month Subscription Plan
summary: Amazon.com Inc. launched two new wearables that use artificial intelligence to record and analyze a person’s day, marking the company’s efforts to reshape Bee, a startup it acquired last year to compete in the hot AI hardware segment.

title: Ripple Opens $9 Billion Perp-Trading Boom to Wall Street Clients
summary: Cryptocurrency firms are increasingly turning to the world of traditional finance for their next leg of growth by positioning themselves as competitors to Wall Street’s entrenched institutional businesses.

title: Ledger Unveils $899 Smartphone-Like Device After $90 Million Crypto Theft
summary: Crypto hardware wallet maker Ledger SAS is launching a smartphone-like device for users seeking extra protection for their digital assets and online activity, in the wake of a security incident involving some of its products.

title: Bonds Seeing ‘Classic Flight to Quality,’ Says JPM’s Berro
summary: Kelsey Berro, fixed income portfolio manager at JPMorgan Asset Management, examines the bond market’s response to US CPI data and the selloff in the artificial-intelligence trade. She speaks on “Bloomberg Brief.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Dyson’s $500 Toothbrush Has One Big Problem: It Doesn’t Work (Yet)
summary: Dyson wants $500 for an AI-powered toothbrush with a camera. But after testing the CameraJet, its high-tech promise was overshadowed by reliability problems. Samantha Kelly reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AI Trade in Fear Phase Right Now, Says Baird’s Mortonson
summary: Ted Mortonson, managing director of technology at Baird, expects that a sharp move lower in the artificial intelligence trade will happen “real quick” if the market moves from fear to a panic phase. He speaks on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Danish Top Court Backs Jail Term in Landmark AI Child-Abuse Case
summary: Denmark’s Supreme Court upheld an 18-month prison sentence for a 31-year-old man for possessing and distributing tens of thousands of AI-generated sexual images depicting children, in a closely watched test of how existing child-abuse laws apply to artificial content.

title: Taiwan Blocks Coinbase, Kalshi Over Suspected Election Bets
summary: Taiwan has blocked the websites of Coinbase Global Inc. and Kalshi Inc. over suspected election betting, weeks before local polls that will test support for President Lai Ching-te’s government.

title: Truecaller India Rival Seeks $1 Billion Valuation in New Funding
summary: Automated call screening app Equal AI is seeking fresh fundraising that could propel it into the league of unicorns, according to its founder, as the startup aims to take on Truecaller.

title: Instagram Fills a Pregnant Reporter’s Feed With a Future to Dread
summary: Social media spotlights the horrors of pregnancies and parenthood gone wrong

title: CoreWeave’s Big Dream Crashes Into Reality as Yields Top 15%
summary: For just about any company, it’d be an audacious thing to say: Find a way to get an investment-grade credit rating, and gain the privilege of borrowing “unlimited” pools of money.

title: Uruguay Hails $5.7 Billion Solar Plant, Data Centers Project
summary: Uruguay President Yamandu Orsi unveiled plans for $5.7 billion in data centers and solar power, touting them as the largest private investment in the South American nation’s history.
